Subject: Post-call: data residency & deployment mode follow-up

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can qualify the best deployment option for FinBank (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Summary from the call
- Primary requirement: customer data and model inputs must remain within the EU for regulatory reasons.
- Secondary: low-latency for EU customers (APAC latency is not critical for this pilot).
- Interested in the Hosted API if we can guarantee EU-only residency and routing; otherwise open to Private VPC.

Questions / asks (to confirm so we can scope next steps)
1) Is EU-only residency strict for ALL traffic (ingest + logs + KV cache + backups), or only for raw customer data?
2) Are there any procurement/timing constraints for a Private deployment (e.g., approved vendors, network isolation policies)?
3) Would you prefer a dedicated capacity contract (reserved GPUs in our EU region) vs a Private VPC with customer-managed networking?

Next steps I propose:
- Ethan (SE) to share a short note on what Hosted EU coverage looks like, and options for Dedicated/Private.
- We’ll send SOC2 summary + short feature brief (attaching).
- Schedule a 60-min architecture workshop with your security and infra team next week to validate network/KMS and failover requirements.

Proposed times: Tue 24 Mar 9–11am CET or Wed 25 Mar 2–4pm CET. Which works best for you?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: EU-only requirement applies to all persisted data (raw inputs, embeddings, logs, backups). Transient compute in non-EU regions for short-lived cache is acceptable only if no user data or logs leave the EU.
- KMS: keys must be customer-managed and hosted in our EU KMS (we prefer Azure Key Vault, will confirm later).
- Procurement: we have a standard vendor onboarding process that takes ~4–6 weeks. Private deployments need an additional security review (another ~2 weeks).
- Preference: if Hosted API can guarantee EU-only data residency and customer-managed KMS integration, that is our preferred path. If not, Private VPC is required.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Can Hosted EU binding include KMS integration (customer-managed) and guarantee logs/backups stay in EU?
2) For Dedicated/reserved capacity in EU, what are the SLAs and committed throughput assumptions?
3) For Private VPC, what are the network connectivity options (S2S VPN, ExpressRoute/Direct Connect) and do you support on-prem air-gapped installs?

Happy to take the architecture workshop — Tue 24 Mar 10:00–11:00 CET works for me. Please include our security lead (I copied IT-GDPR on this thread).

Best,
Anna

Anna — quick technical note to address your questions ahead of the workshop. I’ll keep it high level and we can deep-dive on Tue.

1) Hosted API (EU region):
- We offer hosted endpoints in our EU region (Frankfurt and upcoming Amsterdam region) that can be configured for EU-only data routing.
- Customer-managed KMS: supported via KMS integration APIs and key wrapping; keys remain in your tenant (we store only key reference material in REDWOOD).
- Persistence: logs and backups can be restricted to EU region; we provide options for retention and encrypted backups stored in EU.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Dedicated GPU pools in our EU region with SLA options (99.9% for committed capacity).
- Suitable when you need predictable throughput and isolation without a full Private deployment.

3) Private VPC / On-prem:
- Private control plane with VPC peering / S2S VPN and support for ExpressRoute / Direct Connect.
- On-prem / air-gapped package available for high-regulated customers (requires longer lead time and separate procurement).
- Cross-region routing / DR: We support active/passive failover with EU primary and a secondary region for DR; for strict EU-only residency, DR can be configured within EU-only regions.

Attachments: I've attached the brief and SOC2 summary Marissa mentioned, plus a proposed agenda for the 60-min workshop.

Proposed workshop agenda (Tue 24 Mar 10:00–11:00 CET):
- 10:00–10:10: intros and goals (Marissa + Anna + security lead)
- 10:10–10:30: residency/KMS/network requirements (Ethan + FinBank IT)
- 10:30–10:45: deployment options and tradeoffs (Hosted EU vs Dedicated vs Private)
- 10:45–11:00: next steps / procurement path / timeline (Vivek)

Next logistics: Marissa will send a calendar invite; Vivek will pull together initial ballpark pricing ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private so procurement has context.

— Ethan
